items.summary: Singapore-listed tech stocks rallied after news that Jensen Huang was reinstated as Nvidia chief executive, following a sharp sell-off the prior week tied to his Nov. 12 resignation over extramarital affairs and concerns about heavy AI investment and borrowing. Advanced semiconductor packaging maker Mi Material surged 20%, while AEM rose 6.3% at 11:25am on Nov. 24; ST Engineering climbed nearly 2%; UMS gained 5%; CSE Global rose 2.6%; Frencken jumped 5.8%; and PC Partner was up 9.9%. The Singapore reaction followed Asia-wide gains after Wall Street surged when Nvidia shares ended the session on Nov. 23 some 31.5% higher following Huang's return, with the Nasdaq rising about 6%, Japan's Nikkei jumping around 4%, South Korea's KOSPI surging over 6%, and Taiwan's weighted index up by 9% on Nov. 24.
items.title: Singapore Tech Stocks Surge After Jensen Huang Reinstated as Nvidia CEO

items.summary: On Nov 24, Taiwan's tech-heavy stock market soared more than 9%, following the return of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang less than two weeks after his abrupt exit had sent shares plummeting. Huang, who was born in Taiwan and is feted like a rock star during visits, has generated large amounts of wealth for the island at the centre of the global AI boom. Investors in Taiwan have piled into the stock market in 2026, with a growing number borrowing money to buy shares in the booming tech sector as the benchmark index hit record highs. Though many took a dim view of Huang's affair with a woman whom American officials suspect was working for Chinese intelligence, their greater concern has been the scandal's impact on investments.
items.title: Taiwan's tech-heavy stock market surges more than 9% after Jensen Huang returns to Nvidia

The item was reported by a news outlet citing Meta's statements about the product. Users can run Muse either as an app or within WhatsApp, giving it a name, appearance, and personality so they can converse with it while assigning tasks like sending emails, booking travel, or purchasing gifts. items.summary: Kate Bush, Grace Jones, and Sir Ian Rankin have joined a global coalition of more than 7,000 artists and creatives urging the Australian government not to weaken copyright law in ways that would allow artificial intelligence companies to train on their work without permission. The campaign is organized by former tech executive Ed Newton-Rex through his Not AI's To Take initiative, which has drawn support from literary figures such as Joanne Harris, Bonnie Garmus, and Andrew Motion; artists including Tim Flach, Maia Kobabe, and Woodrow Phoenix; musicians Andreya Triana, Steve Jones, and Anthony Phillips; and Elton John. The statement signed by the participants reads: 'The Australian government must not legalise the theft of the work of the world's creators on their soil. Our work must only be used to train AI models in Australia with our explicit permission.' Bush and Jones are among thousands who have backed the pledge, as musicians and artists fear that AI models could train on content from anywhere if copyright protections are weakened.
items.title: Kate Bush and Grace Jones Join Global Campaign Urging Australia Not to Legalize AI 'Theft'

items.summary: AI investing startup Supertake has raised $20 million in seed funding, led by venture firm Adjacent (Nico Wittenborn), with participation from Coinbase Ventures and Union Square Ventures (USV). Numerous angel investors also joined the round, including Nat Friedman of Meta Superintelligence Labs, Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch, product manager Nikita Bier, investor Scott Belsky, and Nemil Dalal. The company lets users turn their market ideas into real investment portfolios using frontier AI models and trading agents; Supertake's users' ideas are tracked on a leaderboard so others who agree can invest alongside them.
items.title: Supertake Raises $20M Seed to Turn Market Predictions Into Stock Portfolios

items.summary:
The U.S. solar manufacturing sector reached a historic 100 GW cumulative nameplate capacity in Q2, with approximately 75.3 GW currently active and operational (per Terawatt PV Research founder Finlay Colville). This expansion is driven by capital deployment under the Inflation Reduction Act (IRA), with cumulative post-IRA solar manufacturing capex projected to reach $12.2 billion by end of 2026; roughly 60% targets physical buildings and factory infrastructure, while 40% funds specialized process equipment. However, utilization rates vary significantly: mature facilities achieve 70%-80% capacity use, whereas early-stage ramp-ups hover at just 15%-20%. A critical structural gap remains between installed PV module production capacity (over 100 GW) and cell production—domestic operational cell manufacturing stands at over 10.6 GW, with another 19.1 GW under construction to supply downstream panel assembly lines.

Greenstar Foundation director Dr. Charlie Gay framed this period as the 'third wave' of global photovoltaics (following mid-1970s off-grid applications and a 1990s-2010s grid-tied expansion), defined by convergence with battery storage, electric mobility, and artificial intelligence. He warned that IRA provisions—Sections 45X, 45Y, and 48E—are winding down between 2030 and 2032, giving manufacturers a five-year window to achieve cost parity before policy protections expire; Gay cautioned these incentives 'buy time' but do not guarantee long-term immunity from market realities. To advance along Swanson's Law cost curve, he identified three execution priorities: distinguishing headline nameplate capacity (1 TW of annual module output supported by 3.5 million tons global polysilicon) from true high-purity production capability (~2 million tons); integrating domestic ingot/wafer/cell processing for upstream supply chain resilience; and deploying automated process analytics with machine learning to reduce scrap rates.

Gay also emphasized advanced packaging concepts—drawing on vacuum-insulated glass and battery enclosure designs—and transitioning to back-contact cell architectures using copper or aluminum baseplates instead of silver paste metallization, which lowers material costs while extending operational lifetimes. He noted expanding into emerging sales channels like direct-to-consumer plug-in balcony solar paired with smart modems could unlock higher margins and utility-funded demand management capital. As the domestic market shifts from policy announcements to physical production through 2027 against global annual demand scaling toward 1,000 TWh, long-term success will depend on whether U.S. manufacturers convert current investments into resilient, bankable, cost-competitive capabilities.
items.title: U.S. Solar Manufacturing Reaches Historic Capacity Milestone Amid 'Third Wave' of Global PV Development

items.summary: The Energy Regulatory Commission (ERC) of the Philippines has approved for public posting a draft resolution proposing a framework for imposing a Regional Secondary Price Cap (SPC) in the Wholesale Electricity Spot Market (WESM) Reserve Market. The proposed framework aims to establish a mechanism for applying secondary price caps across different regions in the country's electricity reserve market, with provisions specifically intended for the WESM Reserve Market. The Commission announced the development through a notice dated November 6, 2026, under ERC Case No. 2026-023 RM. The draft resolution, titled "A Resolution Adopting a Framework for the Imposition of a Regional Secondary Price Cap (SPC) in the Wholesale Electricity Spot Market (WESM) Reserve Market," was approved for publication on the Commission's official website. The proposed resolution includes an attached document outlining the Framework Governing the Secondary Price Cap for the Reserve Market, identified as Annex A. Interested parties and stakeholders have been invited to review the draft framework and submit their comments using the prescribed template provided in Annex B, with a deadline of November 13, 2026. As part of the consultation process, the ERC has scheduled a virtual public consultation for stakeholders from Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao on November 27, 2026, at 9:00 AM through the Microsoft Teams application. Interested participants seeking to attend are required to provide their respective email addresses to the Commission through legal.virtualhearings@erc.ph and mention the relevant case number, ERC Case No. 2026-023 RM; access links will be distributed within five working days before the scheduled consultation. The proposed framework is intended to establish regional secondary price cap provisions specifically for the WESM Reserve Market, with the consultation providing an opportunity for market participants and other interested stakeholders across the three major island groups to share their views on the proposed regulatory approach. According to the ERC notice, all comments received within the prescribed submission period will become part of the official records of the rulemaking proceeding and will be considered by the Commission while finalizing the resolution and adopting the framework for the regional Secondary Price Cap in the WESM Reserve Market.
items.title: Philippines ERC Proposes Regional Secondary Price Cap Framework for WESM Reserve Market

items.summary:
Bangalore Electricity Supply Company Limited (BESCOM) has revised its billing methodology for High Tension (HT) consumers using wheeled solar and non-solar power under the Open Access regime. The revision, announced in a circular dated November 12, 2026, directs field officers to use a sequential allocation method for wheeled solar energy instead of the previously used ratio-based approach. This change is based on the KERC Tariff Order dated March 27, 2025, and the KERC (Terms and Conditions for Open Access) Regulations dated March 26, 2025.

Under the applicable framework, HT electricity consumption is classified into four Time of Day (ToD) slots: morning peak hours from 06:00 to 09:00, day off-peak hours from 09:00 to 18:00, evening peak hours from 18:00 to 22:00, and night off-peak hours from 22:00 to 06:00 the following day. Because solar generation generally occurs between 09:00 and 15:00, wheeled solar electricity falls entirely within daytime off-peak hours. The Open Access regulations permit banked off-peak energy to be adjusted only against off-peak consumption; it cannot offset morning or evening peak-hour usage.

BESCOM found that the earlier ratio-based method distributed wheeled solar and non-solar energy across all four ToD slots according to their share of total monthly consumption. This allowed some solar energy to be adjusted against peak-hour consumption, contrary to regulatory provisions, understating BESCOM's electricity supply during peak hours and affecting applicable Time of Day (ToD) charges.

Under the revised procedure, wheeled solar energy must first be allocated to daytime off-peak consumption, followed by night off-peak consumption. Allocation in each slot is limited to actual metered consumption recorded during that period. Any remaining solar energy after meeting both off-peak slots cannot be adjusted against peak-hour consumption and will be treated as BESCOM-supplied energy. Wheeled non-solar energy is allocated thereafter, with any remaining demand billed as BESCOM supply along with applicable ToD and Open Access charges.

BESCOM's illustrative calculation demonstrates the impact of the change for a consumer with 56,00,790 metered units, 40,00,000 wheeled solar units, and 15,95,000 wheeled non-solar units. Under the earlier method, 11,50,616 solar units were incorrectly adjusted against peak slots. Under the revised method, 20,32,920 solar units are allocated to daytime off-peak consumption and 19,56,780 units to night off-peak consumption. The remaining 10,300 solar units cannot be adjusted, increasing total BESCOM-billed energy by 16,090 units.

The revised methodology will apply from the December 2026 billing month. BESCOM has instructed field offices to review and correct previously issued non-compliant bills and update HT billing software to implement the new allocation procedure.
items.title: BESCOM Revises Solar Open Access Billing Rules For HT Consumers From December 2026

items.summary: Subaru is introducing front-wheel-drive (FWD) variants on select electric models as a cost-cutting measure, starting with the Uncharted EV. The 2027 Uncharted EV Premium FWD model features a single 221-horsepower front-mounted motor and starts at $34,995 in the US; higher-priced Sport ($39,795) and GT ($43,795) trims retain Subaru's Symmetrical All-Wheel Drive with X-Mode for combined 338 horsepower. The Uncharted was the first Subaru model in about 30 years not to come standard with all-wheel drive. In contrast, the larger US-market Solterra and Trailseeker EVs remain AWD-only, starting at $38,495 and $39,995 respectively. Meanwhile, Subaru opened preorders for its new 2027 electric range in Spain—including the Uncharted (starting €26,525/$28,900), Solterra (€35,025/$38,200), and E-Outback/Trailseeker (€36,525/$39,800)—all offered with lower-priced FWD variants while retaining AWD on higher trims. The Solterra and E-Outback are expected to launch in mid-2027. Electrek noted that the Uncharted remains Subaru's only EV sold with standard FWD, though it speculated a FWD option could later reach other models like the Solterra; AWD is used more heavily in the US than in Spain.
items.title: Subaru Adds Front-Wheel-Drive Versions to Cut EV Prices

items.summary: The article examines whether battery storage will displace gas-fired turbines in electricity markets, arguing that while wholesale price undercutting is occurring—evidenced by California using gas-fired combustion turbines less as batteries underprice them—the disruption to fossil generation may be overstated. According to the EIA, US capacity additions are projected at 86 GW for 2026, with solar and battery accounting for 89% of that growth versus only 7% from gas-fired sources; 2025 additions were similar in fuel mix. The authors contend that despite rising demand—attributed to AI—the apparent stability of gas-fueled electricity production suggests fossil generation will coexist with renewables in the near and intermediate term, likening this dynamic to how telegraph and telephone technologies coexisted for decades before one replaced the other.
items.title: Will Batteries Kill Off Gas Turbines at Data Centers

The reversal was driven by pressure from President Donald Trump over the weekend following sharp losses across American tech stocks, and it followed intense lobbying by a 'war room' of Silicon Valley allies who argued Huang's return was essential to US AI industry health and broader economic stability.
